title: session_window_coverage/v1
description: Issue #2601 (P0): machine-readable session-source coverage and checkpoint-advancement disposition for `run_retrospective.py --since-last-retrospective`. This schema is a NEW, session-window/collector-level vocabulary -- deliberately NOT a reuse of `agent_improvement_candidate_v1.schema.json`'s finding-level `evaluation.source_coverage` (`complete|partial|unavailable|blocked`) nor `latitude_runtime_evidence_v1.schema.json`'s `availability` (`available|unavailable|error`). Both existing vocabularies describe a single already-collected finding/evidence item; this schema describes, for one retrospective run, EVERY required runtime session source's collector-wiring/observation state at once, plus the resulting watermark and checkpoint-advancement decision (AC1). Reused patterns from those two existing schemas (Issue #2601 AC1 requirement): (1) a `reason_code` field that is forced null exactly when its paired status implies success and forced non-null otherwise (mirrors `latitude_runtime_evidence_v1`'s `availability`/`reason_code` forcing invariant), and (2) a closed status enum with an allOf-based forcing invariant (mirrors `agent_improvement_candidate_v1`'s `source_coverage` -> `evaluation_status: indeterminate` forcing invariant). `orchestration.status` (whether the collector/computation pipeline itself completed without a defect) is represented as a field structurally separate from `analysis_completeness` (whether the requested session analysis can be considered complete) -- AC7's core invariant: `orchestration.status: succeeded` is never usable as evidence that `analysis_completeness: complete`.

orchestration.description: AC7: orchestration (pipeline execution) success/failure, kept structurally independent of `analysis_completeness`.

required_sources.description: The session sources this run was asked to analyze (e.g. ["claude_code", "claude_gpt"]). Every entry MUST have a matching key in `source_coverage`.

source_coverage.description: Per-source-id coverage entry. Keys are not restricted to `required_sources` -- a source present in the collector registry but NOT requested this run (e.g. a caller narrowing `--session-sources`) is represented with status `not_requested` rather than omitted, so a reader can always distinguish 'never asked about this source' from 'asked, but collector unwired' (`required`).

selected_session_count.description: Never conflates '0 sessions observed' with 'not observed' (AC2/AC4): non-null only when status is `observed` or (best-effort) `partial`; always null for `required`/`unavailable`/`not_requested`.

analysis_completeness.description: AC2/AC4/AC7: 'complete' iff every required_sources entry has status 'observed' (a coverage-complete run with selected_session_count 0 for every source is still 'complete' -- AC4). 'unavailable' iff no required source is 'observed' or 'partial' (AC2's false-green scenario: zero collector wiring at all). 'degraded' otherwise (mixed coverage, AC3).

cross_runtime_comparison.description: AC3: null only when fewer than 2 sources were required this run (a cross-runtime comparison is not meaningful with a single source). Otherwise always present.

watermark.description: AC5: the from_exclusive/to_inclusive/covered_sources invariant. `covered_sources` names only sources this run actually observed (status 'observed') -- a source that was NOT observed this run is never added to `covered_sources`, so a caller inspecting only the returned watermark can never infer coverage for a source that was not actually confirmed.

checkpoint.description: AC6: durable-checkpoint-advancement disposition. `checkpoint_advanced: true` here is only ever a PROPOSAL -- this schema instance is not itself the durable persistence write (that requires a separately authorized publish channel, mirroring `PublishRequest.authorization_required`); `blocked_no_publish_authorization` makes that distinction explicit rather than reporting a proposal as an already-durable checkpoint (AC6).
